## About this dataset

How aquatic primary productivity influences the carbon (C) sequestering capacity of wetlands is uncertain. We evaluated the magnitude and variability in aquatic C dynamics and compared them to net ecosystem CO2 exchange (NEE) and ecosystem respiration (Reco) rates within calcareous freshwater wetlands in Everglades National Park that vary in hydroperiod. We continuously recorded 30-minute measurements of dissolved oxygen (DO), water level, water temperature, and photosynthetically active radiation (PAR). These measurements were coupled with ecosystem CO2 fluxes over 5 years (2012-2016) in a long-hydroperiod peat-rich, freshwater marsh and a short-hydroperiod, freshwater marl prairie. Daily net aquatic primary productivity (NAPP) rates indicated both wetlands were generally net heterotrophic. Net aquatic primary productivity accounted for 4-5% of the deviance explained in NEE rates.

`Date` · `Water_Level` · `Temperature` · `NEE` · `Reco` · `GEE` · `Precipitation` · `PAR` · `NAP` · `GAP` · `AR`

_Units, definitions and uncertainty are documented in the archived metadata (EML)._

## Research applications

- Linking aquatic metabolism to net ecosystem exchange in wetlands

## Known limitations

- Two sites in Everglades National Park
